issues.title: parser: parseRows turns an empty line into a row with one empty field
issues.body: `parseRows` at `src/parser/read.ts:57` turns an empty line into a row with one empty field, so a text that ends with a line break gets an empty last row. Done when `parseRows` gives no row for an empty line.

issues.title: parser: a line break inside a quoted field splits the row in two
issues.body:
Where: `src/parser/read.ts:59` (`parseRows`) and `src/import-table.ts:5` (`importTable`).

Both functions split the text on line breaks before they read quotes. A quoted field that holds a line break, which RFC 4180 allows and spreadsheet apps write for a cell with several lines, becomes two broken rows. `parseRows(line1\nline2,x)` gives `[[line1'], ['line2, x]]`, not `[[line1nline2, x]]`. Since #91, an empty line inside a quoted field is also dropped with no error.

Why not in the fix of #91: it needs a parser that reads quotes across lines. That is a new design, larger than the fix.

issues.title: parser: splitLine drops an empty last field, so the row loses a column
issues.body:
Where: `src/parser/split.ts:4` (`splitLine`), used by `importTable` in `src/import-table.ts`.

`splitLine` removes the last field when it is empty. `importTable('a,b,c\n1,2,')` gives `[['a','b','c'], ['1','2']]`: the second row has one column less than the header. `parseRows` keeps the field: `['1','2','']`.

Why not in the fix of #91: the `pop` looks intended for a closing comma, so the fix needs a decision on what a closing comma means.

issues.title: parser: importTable and parseRows are two CSV parsers with different rules
issues.body:
Where: `src/import-table.ts:4` (`importTable` with `splitLine` from `src/parser/split.ts`) and `src/parser/read.ts:57` (`parseRows`).

The two functions read the same CSV text in two ways. `parseRows` splits fields on a comma or a tab and removes quotes. `importTable` splits only on a comma, keeps the quotes and drops an empty last field. The fix of #91 had to be written twice, once in each. Each next fix of line handling must also be written twice, and the two can drift.

Why not in the fix of #91: making `importTable` use `parseRows` changes the output of `importTable` for tabs, quotes and closing commas. That needs a decision on which rules are correct.

issues.title: parser: a lone CR line break is not read as a line break
issues.body:
Where: `src/parser/read.ts:59` (`parseRows`) and `src/import-table.ts:5` (`importTable`).

Since #91, both functions split lines on `\r?\n`. A text with a CR alone between lines, as old Mac files have, is read as one line: `parseRows('a,b\rc,d')` gives `[['a', 'b\rc', 'd']]`.

Why not in the fix of #91: #91 is about empty lines. There is no sample of real input files to show whether this form occurs.

issues.title: README: the install command says npm instal, which fails
issues.body:
Where: `README.md:3`.

The README says `npm instal shop`. The npm command is `install`, so the command as written fails.

Why not in the fix of #91: the README is outside the parser module that #91 changes.

issues.title: parser: a UTF-8 BOM stays in the first field of the first row
issues.body:
Where: `src/parser/read.ts:59` (`parseRows`) and `src/import-table.ts:5` (`importTable`).

Neither function removes a byte order mark at the start of the text. Spreadsheet apps write one in "CSV UTF-8" files. For a text that starts with U+FEFF and then `name,age`, the first field of the first row is U+FEFF followed by `name`, so a look-up of the header `name` fails.

Why not in the fix of #91: it is a different defect from empty lines.
